newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly higher.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly higher Friday, except for palladium, after the complex recovered from a midday dip.

Weakness in US stocks and bonds this week provided some support for hard assets like gold and silver, analysts said, after US Federal Reserve chairman Greenspan again warned about excessive valuations and suggested interest rates may need to be raised pre-emptively to combat potential inflation.
But profit taking and liquidation of near-record short positions by funds continued to drive the rally in gold, analysts said.

"Gold ended near its session highs, after breaking out of an intraday consolidation pattern, with fund brokers buying two or three thousand lots in the last hour alone," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said.
"The outlook is positive, but the RSI (relative strength indicator) is getting into overbought zones," he said.
COMEX April gold settled up $4.10 an ounce at $365.10, after seeing a session high at $365.50, the highest level seen since January 3. Estimated total volume was 56,000 lots.
The rally this week has been driven by fund shortcovering, with COMEX gold open interest down a further 6,575 lots Thursday to 175,737, after falling from a high of 199,718 on February 13.
Spot gold bullion ended quoted $363.00/50, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $358.20, and the New York close Thursday at $358.90/40.
Gold has been recovering faster than silver this week, with the spot gold/silver ratio around 68.3 at the close, from a 22 month low at 66.1 on February 17.

Friday was also first notice day for COMEX March silver which ended up 6.7 cents at $5.320, but the more active May silver contract ended up 6.5 cents at $5.375 after seeing a session high at $5.380, just below Thursday's six month high.
Meanwhile, platinum and palladium saw a correction Friday, after leading the complex up earlier this week on concerns about Russian supply problems.

NYMEX April platinum ended up 10 cents at $396.50, but well off the day's highs at $415.00 an ounce. In the physical market platinum fixed at $398.75 in London Friday, a new seven month high, catching up with the jump in NYMEX platinum futures Thursday.
The April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread slipped to $31.00 an ounce from a contract high at $35.30 Thursday.
NYMEX March palladium ended down $2.60 an ounce ahead of first notice day Monday, while the more active June palladium contract ended down $2.40 at $155.00.

News of significant imports of platinum and palladium into Japan in January, including supplies from Russia, suggested Japanese stocks may not have been drawn down as much as earlier expected, analysts said.
But earlier this week a spokesman for Russia's metal export agency, Almaz, said it was unlikely there would be any platinum group metal supplies to Japan in March and possibly none in April either.
"Several factors contributed to the increase in prices this week," CPM Group analyst Ted Kempf said.
"There have been no shipments of palladium to Japan since January causing many fabricators to turn to the spot market for the metal they need."
Russia is the world's main supplier of palladium and the second largest supplier of platinum, while Japan is the world's largest consumer of both metals.
But the annual Russian/Japanese supply contract talks broke down last Decemmber and workers at Russia's Norilsk mine have threatened to strike from March 15 over pay arrears.
"Another factor is the upcoming first notice day for March palladium with the combination of shorts attempting to cover positions and the addition of new longs in the market pushing prices up."
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641
